sentences.text: Shekhahmed vs State Of Karnataka on 2 December, 2025

Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No(s). Of 2025

[ARISING OUT OF SLP (CRIMINAL) No. of 2025  @ Arising out of Diary No. 38118 Of 2025]
 SHEKHAHMED .APPELLANT  VERSUS  STATE OF KARNATAKA .RESPONDENT  ORDER 1.
Leave granted.

2. The present appeal has been filed against the judgment of the High Court1 in Criminal Revision Petition No.100246 of 2019 whereby the conviction of the appellant under Sections 279 and 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 2 was upheld.
The appellant was awarded imprisonment for a period of six months for the offence punishable under Section 304-A IPC and further sentenced to pay fine of 5000/-.
In default thereof, simple imprisonment for 30 days was awarded.
He was also sentenced to pay fine of 500/- for the offence punishable under Section 187 of the M.V. Act.
In default thereof, simple imprisonment for 10 days was awarded.
1 High Court of Karnataka Circuit Bench at Dharwad 2

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka Circuit Bench at Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For short, the M.V. Act 3.

In the case in hand, on account of the accident which took place on 24.11.2012, FIR (Crime No.182/2012) was registered at Karatagi Police Station, District Koppal, Karnataka on 24.11.2012 against the appellant under Sections 279 and 304-A IPC and also Section 187 of the M.V. Act.

entities.text: Karatagi Police Station, District Koppal, Karnataka
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Trial Court 3, finding the appellant guilty of the offence, convicted him under Sections 279 & 304-A IPC and awarded him sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and further sentenced to pay fine of 5000/-.
In default simple imprisonment for 30 days was awarded.
For the offence punishable under Section 187 of the M.V. Act fine of 500/- was also imposed and in default simple imprisonment for 10 days.
No separate punishment was awarded for conviction under Section 279 IPC.
3.1 In appeal4, the judgment5 convicting the appellant and order of sentence were upheld.

The High Court in Revision Petition filed by the appellant also upheld the conviction,
however, modified the sentence from rigorous imprisonment to simple imprisonment for the same Shekhahmed vs State Of Karnataka on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187410743/
1 period.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is 63 years of age, belonging to a lower economic strata of the society.
Earlier he was working as a driver.
Now, with great 3 Vide Order dated 20.12.2013 in C.C. No.61/2013 5 Dated 17.07.2019 difficulty he is making his two meals a day.
He further submitted that the legal representatives of the deceased have already received compensation under the M.V. Act.
The appellant is ready and willing to pay additional compensation to the family of the deceased, in case, instead of sending him to jail his sentence is reduced to the period already undergone.

5. Noticing the aforesaid statement made by the learned counsel for the appellant at the Bar, on 08.08.2025 this Court impleaded the legal representatives of the deceased as respondents and issued notice to them.
5.1 On 07.10.2025 this Court passed the following order:
The newly added respondents-legal representatives of the deceased are stated to be living in Karatagi, District Koppal, Karnataka.

The Member Secretary of the District Legal Services Committee of Koppal District shall contact the legal representatives of the deceased and co-ordinate for their appearance before this Court through video conferencing on the next date of hearing.

entities.text: District Legal Services Committee of Koppal District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In case, assistance of a counsel is required, the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee may be requested.

5.2 Today, the legal representatives of the deceased namely, Yallamma d/o late Thimmanna (deceased), Basavaraja grand-son of the deceased, Saraswathi & Lakshmi, both grand-daughters of the deceased along with Mr. Mahantesh Sangappa Dargad, Member Secretary,
District Legal Services Authority, Koppal, were connected during hearing through video conferencing.

The family of the deceased admitted that they had received compensation under the M.V. Act.
6.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, in our view, the ends of justice will be met,
keeping in view the status of the appellant, in case he pays a sum of 1,00,000/- to the legal representatives of the deceased.
Out of the aforesaid amount 50,000/- be paid on or before 31.12.2025 whereas another installment of 50,000/- on or before 02.02.2026.
Subject to compliance of the aforesaid conditions the sentence of imprisonment awarded to the appellant is reduced to the period already undergone.
For transfer of compensation in the account of the beneficiary, the appellant may coordinate with the Member Secretary, District Legal Services Authority, Koppal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
